chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:

Indeed, the palm-stick is to be of the measure of a handspan. One is placed from near the collarbone to wherever it reaches, on the side next to the right skin, and the other on the left, from near the collarbone to wherever it reaches, above the shirt.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: It is recommended that he write upon his shirt, his outer wrapping, or the winding-sheet that takes its place, or upon the two palm-sticks with his finger: “So-and-so bears witness that there is no god but Allah.” If that is written with the soil of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام, there is much merit in it. It should not be written with black dye nor with any color from the dyes.

key_terms.التَّرْقُوَةِ: the collarbone, marking the point from which placement begins
key_terms.اللِّفَافَةِ: the wrapping cloth or winding-sheet used in shrouding
key_terms.الْجَرِيدَةَ: the palm-stick placed with the deceased as part of funeral practice
key_terms.الْقَمِيصِ: the shirt or garment of the deceased
key_terms.تُرْبَةِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْ: the soil of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام, used here for writing due to its special merit
key_terms.شِبْرٍ: a handspan, indicating the recommended length
key_terms.يَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: the testimony affirming tawhid to be written for the deceased

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended practices for placing the palm-sticks and writing on the shroud in Shia funeral rites?
ai.summary: This report discusses recommended funerary practices for the deceased, including the placement of the two palm-sticks in the shroud and writing the shahadah on parts of the burial cloth. It also mentions the special merit of using the soil of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام for this writing and prohibits using black dye or colored pigments for it.
